title: An LED on a 3.3 V pin
story: A microcontroller pin set to output-high is a 3.3 V source with about 40 ohm of driver resistance inside the chip. You want a red status LED on it. Pick the series resistor so the LED is clearly lit (2 to 8 mA) and the pin still sits above 3.0 V, a clean logic 1.
hints: The LED keeps roughly 1.8 to 1.9 V across itself. The rest is shared by the 40 ohm driver and your resistor.
I = (3.3 - 1.85) / (40 + R). Then the pin voltage is 3.3 - I x 40.
A tiny resistor gives a big current that also drags the pin down; a huge one gives too little light.
